title: Cardinality is preserved under the successor inclusion
statement: Let $S \subseteq \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ be a finite set of indices, and let $\iota \colon \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\} \hookrightarrow \{0, 1, \dots, n\}$ be the order-preserving inclusion that regards each index as an element of the enlarged range. Then the image $\iota(S)$ has the same cardinality as $S$, that is, $\abs{\iota(S)} = \abs{S}$.
hypotheses_covered: S is a finite subset of the index set Fin n
replaced:
Lifting a set along $\mathrm{castSucc}$ preserves its cardinality:
$|\mathrm{castSucc}(S)| = |S|$.
